blocks.text: Big Pop is a design aesthetic that refers to the loud, high-impact, and clean style of pop culture that emerged in the late 1980s and early 1990s. It features larger-than-life bold graphics, superstars, typography, supermodels, and vibrant color-blocking, preceding the earthy grunge movement look in the mid-90s. It is characterized by slanted, big, animated text overlaying designs, or stretched designs.

Its main focus and style of the Big Pop aesthetic includes leather, bodycon dresses, minimalist color-blocked silhouettes, spandex, stark high-contrast shadows, silhouettes of dancers, a specific focus on the human form/shape, high-energy promotional layouts, and white-void music videos.

The Jumbled Font aesthetic is a distorted, playful, typography design style featuring mixed typefaces, geometrical, stretched letters, symbol substitutions and clashing colors, that was prominent between the mid-1980s to the mid-1990s.
